analyst.summary: Dr Reddy's is living through the earnings cliff its Revlimid (cancer-drug) exclusivity loss was always going to cause -- full-year profit fell about a quarter versus last year, with almost the entire hit landing in a single quarter (Jan-Mar 2026) when the licence protection lapsed. The two businesses meant to replace that profit -- a generic weight-loss injection (semaglutide) and a new biosimilar pipeline -- have each hit a manufacturing or regulatory snag in the past five weeks: a US FDA inspection flagged seven observations (up from five nine months earlier) at the plant making the biosimilar, and a manufacturing quality issue has paused semaglutide supply until around November. The stock has already fallen on this news, but not enough, in our view, to compensate for how little visibility there now is into the next couple of quarters. We rate it Sell, while flagging that the underlying business outside the cliff (India, Europe, the new nicotine-replacement-therapy franchise) is genuinely growing and this is not a call that the company is broken.
